rounds.question: Who lives with you and what does a weekday look like?

answers.text: I live alone, so my weekdays are pretty straightforward. I usually wake up early, around 6 AM, and then I’m out the door by 7 to beat the traffic. I work long hours, about 60 a week, and I spend around 45 minutes commuting each way. After work, I might run some errands or just relax at home since I don’t have anyone else to share my evenings with.

I live with my husband and our two kids, who are 8 and 5. Our weekdays are pretty busy! In the mornings, I usually get up early to make breakfast and pack lunches before getting the kids ready for school. After dropping them off, I spend my day tutoring, which keeps me on my toes. Once the kids are back home, it’s all about homework, dinner, and getting them ready for bed. It feels like a whirlwind sometimes, but I wouldn’t trade it for anything!

I live with my husband and our two kids, who are in their late teens. On a typical weekday, I wake up early to get everyone ready for the day. I usually make breakfast and pack lunches for the kids before I head out to work. My commute is about 15 minutes, which is nice, and then I spend my day at work, managing various projects. After work, I try to spend some time with the family, maybe help with homework or just catch up on our day. It can get a bit hectic, but we make it work!

I live with my husband, our 14-year-old child, and we have a dog. On a typical weekday, my husband leaves for work early in the morning, and I usually get my child ready for school. I help with breakfast and make sure they have everything they need for the day. After they leave, I have some time to myself, which I often use to catch up on work or take care of household tasks. I work part-time as a lawyer, so I balance that with family responsibilities. In the evening, we all have dinner together, and then it's homework time for my child. We try to spend some quality time as a family before bed.

I live with my wife, our 16-year-old child, and two pets—a dog and a cat. On a typical weekday, I get up early to get ready for work while my wife prepares breakfast. My child is usually still getting ready for school, and we all try to sit down together for a quick meal before I head out. I commute about 30 minutes to my job as a software developer, and once I’m back home in the evening, we often have dinner together and help our child with homework. It’s a busy household, but we make it work.

I live with my wife and our three kids, so there are six of us in total. On a typical weekday, I wake up around 6:00 AM, and I usually help get the kids ready for school. They leave by 7:30 AM, and then I head out to work by 8:00 AM. I work about 40 hours a week, so I’m at work from around 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM. I get home around 5:30 PM, and then it’s family time—dinner, helping with homework, and getting everyone ready for bed. It’s a busy routine, but I wouldn’t have it any other way.

rounds.question: Where do you run out of space at home?

answers.text: I run out of space mostly in my living area and kitchen. Since I live alone, I don’t have a lot of furniture, but I still find it cramped sometimes, especially when I try to entertain friends or family. The kitchen can feel cluttered, too, since I don’t have much counter space to work with. I think if I had more room, I’d like to have a dedicated area for hobbies or just a more comfortable space to relax.

For us, space is definitely tight in the kids' bedrooms. They have toys, clothes, and school supplies everywhere, and it feels like we’re constantly trying to find places to store everything. I also wish we had a little more room in the kitchen; it can get crowded when I’m cooking dinner and trying to help the kids with their homework at the same time. I can relate to P003 and P004, who also juggle family responsibilities, but for me, it’s really about managing the chaos that comes with having younger kids.

I can relate to P002's busy household; space can definitely feel tight sometimes. In our home, I’d say we run out of space mainly in the kids' rooms and the common areas. With two teenagers, their stuff seems to multiply! Between school projects, sports equipment, and just general clutter, it can get overwhelming. Plus, our living room sometimes feels cramped when we all gather there, especially when we have friends or family over. I guess I wish we had a bit more storage or a designated area for everything to keep things organized.

I find that we run out of space in our garage and the kids' play area. The garage has become a catch-all for things we don’t use regularly, like seasonal decorations and old furniture. It’s hard to park the cars in there because it’s so cluttered. As for the kids' play area, with my child growing up, we have a lot of toys and sports equipment that just take up too much room. P002 mentioned a busy household, and I can relate to that feeling of needing more space for everything as the family grows.

I can relate to P002’s experience of a busy household. In my case, we definitely run out of space in the common areas, especially the living room and kitchen. With five people and two pets, it can feel cramped, especially during meal times or when everyone is trying to relax after a long day. Our four-bedroom home is great, but we could really use more storage space for all the kids' school supplies, sports equipment, and just general clutter that accumulates. It feels like we’re constantly trying to find a place for everything, which can be frustrating.

For us, space is definitely an issue in the bedrooms. We have two bedrooms for six people, which means the kids are sharing rooms, and it can get pretty cramped. With three kids, it feels like there’s never enough room for their toys, clothes, and school stuff. We also struggle with storage in the kitchen; it’s tough to find space for all the cooking supplies and groceries, especially when we’re trying to prepare meals for a larger family. I can relate to P002’s experience; it can feel overwhelming sometimes trying to keep everything organized.

rounds.question: What makes that situation difficult for you?

answers.text: The tight space makes it difficult to feel comfortable when I have friends over. I want to create a welcoming environment, but it can feel cramped, which makes it hard to relax and enjoy the time together. Plus, in the kitchen, not having enough counter space can be frustrating when I’m trying to cook or prepare meals. It just adds to the stress of daily life when everything feels cluttered.

rounds.question: I'd like to show you an idea. It's called the Tahoe Mini, from Neo Smart Living: a compact 117-square-foot studio, built in a factory, then delivered and installed in your backyard. It isn't an ADU, so there's no kitchen or bathroom. What's your first reaction, and what would you use it for?

stimulus.text:
PRODUCT CONCEPT SHOWN BY THE MODERATOR:
Name: Tahoe Mini by Neo Smart Living
Description: A compact 117-square-foot factory-built studio that is delivered and installed in a backyard. It is not an ADU and has no kitchen or bathroom.
- 117 square feet
- Factory-built; delivered and installed in your backyard
- Not an ADU: no kitchen, no bathroom
Intended for: homeowners with usable outdoor space

answers.text: My first reaction is skepticism. A 117-square-foot space without a kitchen or bathroom seems really limiting. I can see it being useful as a home office or a personal retreat, but without basic amenities, I’m not sure how practical it would be for long-term use. I’d want to know more about how it could enhance my living situation before considering it seriously.

My first reaction is that it sounds really interesting! I can see a lot of potential for it, especially since we’re running out of space in our home. I think it could be a great playroom for the kids or even a quiet space for me to tutor without distractions. Having a dedicated area for activities would definitely help with the clutter in the main living areas. I know it doesn’t have a kitchen or bathroom, but I think it could still serve a lot of purposes, like a home office or a cozy reading nook. I’m definitely open to the idea!

I appreciate the idea behind the Tahoe Mini, but my first reaction is that it might not fit seamlessly into my daily routine. Since it doesn't have a kitchen or bathroom, I’m not sure how practical it would be for everyday use. I guess I could see it as a quiet space for working or maybe a small retreat for my kids when they need a break from the house. But without those essential amenities, I feel like it might just end up being an extra storage space rather than something we actively use. It really depends on how we could integrate it into our already busy lives.

My first reaction is that it seems like an interesting concept, but I have some concerns about its practicality. Without a kitchen or bathroom, it feels more like a glorified shed than a usable space. I can see it being useful as a home office or a quiet retreat for reading or hobbies, but I question how much value it would actually add to my home. Given the cost of real estate and construction, I would want to know if the price reflects the utility and space it offers. I agree with P002 that having a dedicated area for activities is great, but I need to weigh that against what I’d actually get for my investment.

Honestly, my first reaction is skepticism. I understand the appeal of having extra space, especially for a busy household like mine, but I’m not sure how practical this would be without a kitchen or bathroom. It feels like it could be a nice retreat or a place for my child to have their own space for studying or hobbies, but I worry about the lack of essential amenities. Plus, I have concerns about how connected devices might be involved in its operation—I'm not comfortable trusting those technologies in my home. So while I see some potential, I have significant reservations about its overall usefulness for my family.

My first reaction is that it sounds interesting, but I’m a bit skeptical about how practical it would be for my family. With no kitchen or bathroom, I wonder how useful it really would be. I can see it being a nice space for a home office or a kids' play area, but I’d worry it would end up unused like some other things we’ve tried. For it to work for us, it would need to be a space that we could find a reason to use regularly, maybe for hobbies or as a quiet spot for my wife and me to unwind. Otherwise, it might just become another storage area.

Considering it’s a factory-built structure, I’d expect it to be on the higher end of that scale, especially since it’s being delivered and installed. However, without a kitchen or bathroom, I’d want to know if the price reflects its actual utility and how much it could enhance my living space.
